c.tagline: Iran's holiest city, drawing millions to the golden shrine of Imam Reza.

taxi.fareNote: Use the Snapp or Tapsi apps for fair fixed fares. Foreign bank cards don't work in Iran, so carry cash (rials); app wallets are topped up with cash. Agree a price before boarding street or shared taxis.

emergency.note: Fire: 125. English-speaking operators are not guaranteed; hotel staff can assist.

avoid.reason: Dense crowds around the Imam Reza shrine and Bazar-e Reza attract pickpockets; keep valuables secured.

hood_desc: The pedestrianized precinct immediately around the vast Imam Reza shrine complex, with Goharshad Mosque, the Reza Bazaar and Nader Shah's tomb steps away; where most pilgrims base themselves to be within walking distance of the haram.
The busy commercial artery running from the shrine, packed with hotels, shopping arcades, saffron and souvenir shops and restaurants; convenient and lively, ideal for first-time visitors.
Older lanes northwest of the shrine along Nawab Safavi and Tabarsi streets, dense with budget guesthouses, pilgrim eateries and local markets; authentic and inexpensive.
Mashhad's upscale modern district along tree-lined Sajjad Boulevard, known for its smart restaurants, cafes and boutiques; a change of pace from the shrine crowds for dining out.
A greener residential area around Koohsangi Park stretching toward Vakilabad, with parks, quieter hotels and family homes away from the pilgrim bustle.

water.note: Tap water is chlorinated and generally safe, though many visitors prefer bottled.

transit.pay: Fares use a rechargeable Man-Card (Mashhad transit smart card) tapped at metro gates and on buses; single tickets are sold at metro stations. Foreign bank cards don't work in Iran, so top the card up with cash.
transit.hours: Metro and buses run roughly 06:00-22:00; there is no overnight service, so late-night travelers rely on Snapp or Tapsi.
transit.note: The Metro links the airport and the shrine area; the streets immediately around the Imam Reza shrine are pedestrianized and best explored on foot.

train: Mashhad Railway Station - domestic services to Tehran, Isfahan, Yazd and other cities
bus: Mashhad Central Bus Terminal (Imam Reza Terminal) - intercity coaches across Iran

transit.m: Mashhad Metro / airport bus toward the shrine area (30-40 min)
Snapp / Tapsi to the shrine area (20-30 min)

tip.r: Rounding up is appreciated in taxis and restaurants; upscale venues may add a service charge. Not deeply ingrained but increasingly common in tourist-facing places.

landmarks: Imam Reza Holy Shrine
One of Islam's largest shrine complexes, a dazzling city of golden domes, mirrored halls and vast courtyards drawing 25 million pilgrims yearly.
Goharshad Mosque
A 15th-century Timurid masterpiece within the shrine complex, its turquoise dome and mosaic-tiled iwans rank among Persia's supreme architectural works.
Tomb of Ferdowsi (Tus)
A marble Achaemenid-style mausoleum outside Mashhad honoring the poet of the Shahnameh, whose verses safeguarded the Persian language itself.
Nader Shah Mausoleum
The bold stone tomb-museum of Persia's 18th-century conqueror, capped by a dramatic bronze statue of Nader on horseback.
Bazaar Reza
A kilometer-long covered bazaar beside the shrine, glittering with saffron, turquoise jewelry and prayer rugs, the classic Mashhad souvenir hunt.
Central Museum of Astan Quds Razavi
The shrine's treasury museum displays priceless carpets, illuminated Qurans and centuries of gifts bestowed upon Imam Reza's sanctuary.
Kooh Sangi Park
Mashhad's beloved hillside park, where twin rocky crags, fountains and evening promenades deliver sweeping views over the pilgrimage city.
Gonbad-e Sabz (Green Dome)
A serene Safavid-era mausoleum of the mystic Sheikh Mohammad Momen, its green-tiled dome a quiet counterpoint to the shrine's grandeur.
Harooniyeh Monument (Tus)
A hulking brick dome near Ferdowsi's tomb, traditionally linked to Harun al-Rashid and honoring the theologian al-Ghazali nearby.
Kang Village
A stepped Zoroastrian-era mountain village in the Binalud foothills, its stacked mud-brick homes often likened to a miniature Masuleh.

dom.op: Raja Passenger Trains (Islamic Republic of Iran Railways)

train.note: Mashhad is the busiest passenger rail destination in Iran, fed by pilgrim traffic to the Imam Reza shrine, and the station on the western side of the city has overnight departures to Tehran (roughly 11-12 hours) plus services from Isfahan, Shiraz, Tabriz, Yazd, Kerman, Ahvaz and Bandar Abbas. Alongside state operator Raja, private companies such as Fadak, Safir and Noor al-Reza run higher-grade sleepers on the Tehran route, and the good ones sell out well ahead around Nowruz and religious holidays. Booking at https://www.raja.ir/ generally needs an Iranian bank card and an Iranian IP address, so foreign visitors normally buy through a local travel agency or at the station. There are no international trains: the Tehran-Ankara Trans-Asia Express never resumed after the pandemic, and the Mashhad-Sarakhs line to Turkmenistan carries no scheduled passenger service.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches leave from Mashhad's main terminal (Terminal-e Mosaferbari) south-west of the shrine, where dozens of Iranian companies including Seir-o-Safar, Hamsafar and Royal Safar have counters; tickets are bought at the counter or through Iranian booking apps, which usually require an Iranian card. Tehran is about 12 hours by VIP coach, Isfahan around 15 and Tabriz well over 20. Cross-border services to Herat via Taybad and to Ashgabat via Bajgiran do operate but are irregular and depend heavily on the security and visa situation of the day, so confirm locally before relying on them; Turkmen visas in particular must be arranged well in advance. For most foreign visitors the domestic bus network is cheap, frequent and more comfortable than the equivalent train.

ferry.note: Mashhad lies in north-eastern Iran roughly 700 km from the Caspian and much further from the Persian Gulf, with no navigable waterway, so there are no ferry services.

half.name: Torghabeh
half.blurb: A mountain resort village about 20 minutes west, with terraced tea houses, a cable car, and streamside walking trails.

full.name: Kalat
full.blurb: A remote border town about 2.5 hours away, home to Nader Shah's unfinished 18th-century Sun Palace mausoleum.
